basics.description: **Sentinel content for Abstract data: rules and workbooks** Abstract Security: a security data pipeline and agentic SIEM in one platform. A self-contained approximation of the Abstract Microsoft Sentinel solution that installs connector tiles, an ASIM parser function, analytics and automation rules, hunting queries, workbooks and playbooks into an existing Sentinel workspace. Sufficient for a lab or private install; not a substitute for the certified Content Hub package. The Abstract connector tiles, parser, rules, workbooks and playbooks, into a workspace that already runs Microsoft Sentinel.

options.text: The Abstract connector tiles, parser, rules, workbooks and playbooks, into a workspace that already runs Microsoft Sentinel.

basics.label: Setup depth
basics.toolTip: Recommended settings shows only what most deployments set and keeps every other setting at its default. Show every setting adds a More settings section to each tab. Hidden settings are sent with their defaults, so either choice deploys.

options.text: Questions or help with this deployment: email support@abstract.security or use the contact page at https://www.abstract.security/contact-us.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', subscription().subscriptionId, '" and type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces" and resourceGroup =~ "', resourceGroup().name, '" | project name, location, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, id = tolower(id) | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type =~ "microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions" and name startswith "SecurityInsights(" | project id = tolower(tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId)), hasSentinel = 1) on id | extend sentinel = iff(isnotnull(hasSentinel), "yes", "no") | project name, location, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, id, sentinel | order by name asc')]

elements.toolTip: The workspace the content is installed into. It must already run Microsoft Sentinel and be in this resource group, because every item is created under it. Nothing it already has is changed; the content only adds its own items. Find it: Azure portal > Microsoft Sentinel, the workspace name. Example: sentinel-prod. The list is read live from Azure Resource Graph.

Installs the Abstract Security data connector tiles, the ASim_AbstractEvent parser, two analytics rules and three automation rules (all installed disabled), three hunting queries, the Pipeline Overview and Value & ROI workbooks, and three playbooks. Your own rules, workbooks and playbooks are not touched.

This template installs content only. Deploy the Abstract data plane (Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule and AbstractEventLogs_CL) separately with the Sentinel destination template; the connector tile and workbooks read what it creates.

elements.name: customTableName
elements.label: Abstract table read by the content
elements.toolTip: The custom table the Abstract destination writes to, which the connector tile, the parser and the workbooks read. Change it only if the data plane was deployed with another table name; a wrong name leaves the content reading an empty table. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables. Example: AbstractEventLogs_CL. Default: AbstractEventLogs_CL.

validations.message: Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter and ending in _CL.

options.text: The playbooks read the Abstract API key from a Key Vault secret at run time. Later installs them without one: they fail at their first Abstract call until a secret is set. In a new or an existing Key Vault, the key you enter is sent only as a secure parameter, never in the outputs or the deployment history, and the deployment can grant each playbook its two roles. After the install, authorize each playbook's Microsoft Sentinel API connection.

elements.name: abstractVendorAccountId
elements.label: Abstract vendor account ID
elements.toolTip: Your Abstract tenant's vendor account ID, which the playbooks send as x-as-vendor-account-id to select your tenant. Leave it empty to set it later in each playbook's parameters; until then the playbooks' Abstract calls fail. Find it: Abstract > your account settings, or ask Abstract. Example: AbCdEf1234.

validations.message: No spaces or quotes, or empty to set it later.

elements.placeholder: Leave empty to set it later

elements.name: apiKeyMode
elements.label: Store my Abstract API key now
elements.toolTip: Where the playbooks read the Abstract API key at run time. Later stores nothing and asks for nothing, so the deployment never waits on a key; the playbooks fail at their first Abstract call until a secret is set. In a new Key Vault creates a vault in this resource group and writes the key you enter into it; in an existing Key Vault writes it into a vault in this resource group. With either, the key travels only as a secure parameter, never in the outputs or the deployment history, and the deployment can grant each playbook the two roles it needs. I already have a secret points the playbooks at a secret you made yourself, and you grant their roles. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets. Default: Later.

allowedValues.label: In an existing Key Vault in this resource group

elements.name: abstractApiKey
elements.toolTip: The API key Abstract issued for your tenant. The deployment writes it into the Key Vault as a secret, which the playbooks read at run time. Required when the key is stored in a new or existing Key Vault, and not used otherwise. It is a secure parameter: it never appears in the deployment's inputs, outputs or history. A rerun that stores the key needs it again and writes a new version of the secret. Anyone who can read the secret can call the Abstract API as your tenant. Find it: The API key Abstract issued for your tenant, or ask Abstract.

constraints.validationMessage: The key as Abstract gave it, with no spaces.

elements.name: keyVaultNameNew
elements.label: New Key Vault name
elements.toolTip: The name of the vault this deployment creates in this resource group, in the resource group's region, with Azure RBAC permissions, soft delete (7 days) and purge protection on. Key Vault names are unique across Azure and cannot be changed. Purge protection keeps a deleted vault, and its name, for 7 days: after a resource group or vault is deleted the same name fails until then, so pick another. A vault already in this resource group is refused: creating it again would reset its network settings, so choose In an existing Key Vault. The form checks the name with Azure, and against the deleted vaults of this subscription, as you type. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults, and Key vaults > Manage deleted vaults. Example: abstract-sentinel-kv.

validations.message: 3 to 24 letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, ending with a letter or digit, no two hyphens in a row.
A Key Vault with this name is already in this resource group. Choose In an existing Key Vault and pick it: creating it again would reset its network settings to public access.

A deleted Key Vault with this name is still held under purge protection (up to 7 days after it was deleted), so Azure refuses the name. Pick another name, or recover that vault and choose In an existing Key Vault.

Azure says this Key Vault name is taken (a vault anywhere in Azure, possibly one an earlier run created here). Pick another name, or choose In an existing Key Vault to reuse a vault in this resource group.

elements.label: Existing Key Vault in this resource group

A vault that uses access policies instead of Azure RBAC permissions does not take the role grants. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults, filtered to this resource group. Example: abstract-sentinel-kv.

After the deployment, add an access policy with the Get secret permission for each playbook (Key vaults > the vault > Access policies), or pick a vault that uses Azure role-based access control.

elements.name: grantPlaybookRoles
elements.label: Grant the playbooks their roles
elements.toolTip: Gives each playbook's managed identity Key Vault Secrets User on the stored secret only (not the vault) and Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the workspace, the two roles the playbooks need to run. Applies only when the deployment stores the key; with no Key Vault, nothing is granted. Needs Owner, or User Access Administrator, on this resource group, or the deployment fails. Turn it off only if your team grants roles another way; until both roles are granted, the playbooks fail. It is the master switch: the two switches below leave out one role each. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Access control (IAM), and the workspace > Access control (IAM). Default: on.

elements.name: keyVaultSecretUriMode
elements.label: How to find your secret
elements.toolTip: Pick a secret lists the Key Vaults you can see, in every subscription, and the secrets of the one you choose. Enter the URI is for a vault the list does not show, or a secret you cannot list. The key itself never enters this deployment: the playbooks read the secret at run time. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets. Default: Pick a secret.

Example: abstract-api-key.

On a rerun that installs the playbooks again, give the URI the playbooks use now (the abstractApiKeySecretUri output of the earlier deployment): a rerun that neither stores the key nor gives a URI sets the playbooks' secret URI to empty. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Secret Identifier, then add ?api-version=7.4. Example: https://myvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/abstract-api-key?api-version=7.4.

validations.message: A Key Vault secret URI with the API version, such as https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<name>?api-version=7.4, or empty.

elements.toolTip: The name of the Key Vault secret that holds the Abstract API key, 1 to 127 letters, digits and hyphens. Used only when the deployment stores the key. A secret of that name already in the vault gets a new version, and the playbooks read the latest version. Keep the default unless your naming standard says otherwise. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets. Example: abstract-api-key. Default: abstract-api-key.

elements.name: abstractBaseUrl
elements.label: Abstract API base URL
elements.toolTip: The Abstract API the playbooks call. Change it only for a non-production Abstract environment, as Abstract tells you. A wrong URL makes every playbook call fail. Find it: The address of your Abstract API, as given by Abstract. Example: https://api.abstractsecurity.app. Default: https://api.abstractsecurity.app.

validations.message: An https:// URL with no path or trailing slash.
